top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rewards three originating ideas with separable roles: a tractable time-dependent pricing device, staggered contracts with policy-rule analysis, and a microfounded welfare-based framework for evaluating policy. Later work on estimation, state dependence and heterogeneity builds on this structure and uses it as its reference point. The ideas are 25 to 45 years old, and no recent prize covers pricing frictions or policy rules. Attribution is the main cost, because Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are excluded, and the Fischer and Phelps priority questions are unresolved. The post-2021 and state-dependent-pricing evidence limits what a citation can claim, so it should credit originating ideas as an analytical benchmark and make no claim about forecasting performance. I rank P002 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) second for its cleaner credit and its mature framework, despite weaker cross-country identification and the neighbouring 2024 prize. I rank P003 (Helpman, Melitz) third for a clean two-name core and direct firm-level testing, offset by credit omissions (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum) and its closeness to the 2008 trade prize. All three are mature and defensible, so I rank no award last. This ranking rests on the supplied evidence and general knowledge, not on independent verification, and it does not count support totals as merit.
recusal_note: Disclosed, not adjudicated. My profile documents no tie to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Helpman or Melitz. I co-authored the menu-costs paper with Richard Friberg and Tore Ellingsen, which is adjacent to the price-setting topics in P001. I am a frequent co-author and IIES colleague of Per Krusell and Timo Boppart, and Krusell works on heterogeneous-agent macro, a successor literature to P001. Other members' files report IIES links with Torsten Persson (P002), but my profile does not document any. My research in dynamic macroeconomics and public finance is close in field to P001 and P002, so I apply the common criteria.
